{ "rules": [
    "Model forecasts are consistently below true outcomes, showing a persistent downward bias that increases with longer horizons as true prices continue rising.",
    "Sentiment turning positive ( > 0) correlates with model undershoot, especially in the first 10-15 day forecast horizon where bias is most pronounced.",
    "The forecast gap between model and true outcomes expands from ~0.4-0.6 on day 1 to ~1.0-2.0 by day 15-20, indicating lag that compounds over time.",
    "When sentiment is negative ( < 0), model forecasts overestimate prices relative to true outcomes, creating a reverse bias in the opposite direction.",
    "Prices show clear mean-reversion in model forecasts (returning to center of history range) while true outcomes continue trending away from recent levels.",
    "Sentiment momentum (changing from negative to positive or vice versa) amplifies the forecast-error magnitude by approximately 20-30% compared to static sentiment values.",
    "Model forecasts lack volatility relative to true outcomes, showing smoother trajectories that don't capture the price swings observed in actual carbon market data."
] }
